profile.subject: Leonardo da Vinci
profile.overview: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian Renaissance painter and engineer who worked in Florence and Milan and spent his last years in France. He painted the **Mona Lisa** and **The Last Supper**, and filled notebooks with studies of subjects as different as the valves of the heart and the flight of birds.

key_moments.title: An angel in Verrocchio’s workshop
key_moments.text: Leonardo trained in the Florence workshop of **Andrea del Verrocchio**. Both artists worked on The Baptism of Christ, a panel with two angels kneeling by the river. The Uffizi credits Leonardo with the angel on the left and suggests that his hand may also be visible in the river landscape behind it.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci trained in Andrea del Verrocchio’s workshop in Florence.
Leonardo da Vinci and Andrea del Verrocchio both worked on The Baptism of Christ, dated to about 1470–1475.
The Uffizi attributes the angel on the left of The Baptism of Christ to Leonardo da Vinci and considers that Leonardo may also have painted the river landscape.

key_moments.title: The Last Supper in Milan
key_moments.text: For **Ludovico Sforza**, Leonardo painted the wall of a dining hall at Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. The painted room seems to extend the real one. Working on dry plaster gave Leonardo time to revise the scene, but the same technique contributed to early paint loss.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper around 1494–1498 for Ludovico Sforza in the dining hall of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan.
The perspective of The Last Supper makes the painted chamber seem to extend the dining hall.
Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper on dry plaster to allow changes.
The dry technique contributed to pigment loss soon after The Last Supper was finished.

key_moments.title: Leonardo begins the Mona Lisa
key_moments.text: The Louvre dates the start of Leonardo’s portrait of **Lisa Gherardini**, the wife of a Florentine silk merchant, to around 1503. He painted her turning toward the viewer and used glazes to soften the edges of her features. He kept the portrait for years, continuing to work on it.
claims: The Louvre dates the start of Leonardo da Vinci’s Mona Lisa to around 1503.
The Mona Lisa depicts Lisa Gherardini, the wife of the Florentine silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo.
Leonardo da Vinci depicted Lisa Gherardini turning toward the viewer and used glazes to soften edges in the Mona Lisa.
Leonardo da Vinci kept the Mona Lisa for years and continued to work on it.

key_moments.title: A new patron in France
key_moments.text: **Francis I** invited Leonardo to France, where he settled at the Clos Lucé in Amboise and served the king as a painter, architect and engineer. Leonardo studied the region’s waterways and envisioned a royal palace and drew up plans for a town at Romorantin.
claims: Francis I invited Leonardo da Vinci to France in 1516, and Leonardo da Vinci settled at the Clos Lucé in Amboise.
Leonardo da Vinci served Francis I as painter, architect and engineer.
Leonardo da Vinci studied local waterways, envisioned a royal palace and drew up plans for a town at Romorantin.

deep_facts.text: While surveying strongholds for Cesare Borgia in 1502, Leonardo drew **a map of Imola** that set the town’s streets inside a circle. Around the rim he wrote the names of winds at the eight points of the compass.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci drew a plan of Imola in 1502 while surveying strongholds for Cesare Borgia.
Leonardo da Vinci drew Imola’s street plan inside a circle and wrote wind names at the eight compass points.

deep_facts.text: Leonardo studied the hearts of oxen and sketched a mould for a **glass model** to study the aortic valve. In his notes, he linked the valve’s closing to eddies in the blood. The Royal Collection describes him using the model. A 2002 study cited laboratory flow images as evidence that he may have built it, leaving the question open.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci studied the heart valves of oxen and sketched a mould for a glass model to study the aortic valve.
Leonardo da Vinci linked eddies in the blood to the closing of the aortic valve.
The Royal Collection describes Leonardo da Vinci using the glass model.
A 2002 study cited laboratory flow images as evidence that Leonardo da Vinci may have built the glass model.

deep_facts.text: Leonardo’s **Codex on the Flight of Birds** puts notes on birds and flying machines into his right-to-left mirror script. He assembled it from partly used sheets, some of them already marked with reddish sketches of plants.
claims: Leonardo da Vinci’s Codex on the Flight of Birds contains mirror writing and studies of bird flight and flying machines.
Leonardo da Vinci compiled the Codex on the Flight of Birds from partly used sheets that still show reddish sketches, including sketches of plants.

issues: connections.1.connection: The excerpts date Leonardo’s move or acceptance to 1516. They leave the date Francis issued the invitation unstated. Say “Leonardo moved to France at his invitation in 1516 and served him as painter, architect and engineer.”

connections.2.connection: The evidence places Leonardo in Borgia’s service in Romagna and the Imola map among his surveys for Borgia. Add evidence for the implied location of Imola within Romagna or say “Employed Leonardo as an architect and engineer while Leonardo was surveying strongholds and mapping Imola.”

deep_facts.2.text: The Musei Reali source establishes that the manuscript was assembled from partly used sheets. It leaves the assembler unnamed. Say “The codex was assembled from partly used sheets” unless the evidence specifically attributes assembly to Leonardo.

blockers: key_moments.0.text: The finding for the two kneeling angels omits that The Baptism of Christ was painted on a panel. Add a finding quoting the Uffizi medium, “Tempera and oil on panel”.
key_moments.0.text: The findings omit the position of the river landscape behind the left angel. Anchor this placement to a readable source or omit “behind it”.

connections.1.connection: The excerpts date Leonardo’s move or acceptance to 1516. They leave the date Francis issued the invitation unstated. Say “Leonardo moved to France at his invitation in 1516 and served him as painter, architect and engineer.”

connections.2.connection: The evidence places Leonardo in Borgia’s service in Romagna and the Imola map among his surveys for Borgia. Add evidence for the implied location of Imola within Romagna or say “Employed Leonardo as an architect and engineer while Leonardo was surveying strongholds and mapping Imola.”

deep_facts.1.text: The Gharib quotation confirms that Leonardo mentioned a glass model. For independent corroboration of the specific mould sketch and its intended use, add another original source or attribute that detail explicitly to the Royal Collection’s reading of the extant drawing. Preserve the attributed disagreement about whether Leonardo built the model.

deep_facts.2.text: The Musei Reali source establishes that the manuscript was assembled from partly used sheets. It leaves the assembler unnamed. Say “The codex was assembled from partly used sheets” unless the evidence specifically attributes assembly to Leonardo.
